text: Interpret signs, panels, markings and signals together, including authorised directions.

Follow the traffic instructions that apply to you. Where an instruction differs from a general traffic rule, the instruction governs. A steady traffic-light indication takes precedence over a yield or stop sign; a police officer's direction takes precedence over the rules and ordinary traffic instructions. This is not a rule that a green signal cancels every other restriction. Authorised guards also give traffic directions that must be followed. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §§2–4
Authorised directions Separate examples. A static picture does not show the complete movement; read the description and the official instruction.

Traffic approaching the officer from the front or rear must stop; traffic approaching from the sides may proceed. The officer's continuing orientation matters even after the arm movement. Officer faces the viewer with one arm extended sideways.

Read the current signs and conditions rather than selecting a speed from the road’s appearance. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §17, chapter 4 §20 and chapter 9 §1

text: A police officer signals you to stop while your traffic light is green. What should you do?
The officer's instruction has higher priority than the light.
B. Stop as directed by the officer.
A police officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals, signs and general rules.
C. Continue if the road looks clear
A clear road does not cancel the instruction.
D. Stop only if there is a stop sign
A police officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals, signs and general rules.

Chapter 9 §§1–2 confirms motorway/expressway eligibility and movement restrictions. No legal exception is treated as proof that a manoeuvre is safe.
Turning/leaving road must protect oncoming and same-direction/rear traffic; turning around must avoid danger/obstruction; motorway/expressway turnaround and reversing prohibited.

Chapter 3 §§1, 14–15 and 68–72 supports fitness, visibility-based speed and lighting duties, including main-beam dazzle restrictions and fog-light combinations. Chapter 4 §10e supports the equipment-use limits; §§18a–18d confirms the winter-tyre framework for the ordinary light-vehicle case. Current provisions are used, not future amendments.

Chapter 3 §§78–83 confirms securing, unobstructed controls/signals and projection marking. Chapter 4 §§15–17 confirms ordinary width/length restrictions and exemptions. Chapter 4 §20 version applicable before 1 December 2026 supports the scoped 80/40/30 trailer limits; future amendment not applied early. Chapter 3 §14 supports appropriate speed.
Safe-speed adaptation depends on road/weather/visibility/load and foreseeable stopping distance.

Chapter 3 sections 2 and 14 support following distance and safe speed/control. Chapter 4 sections 22–24a supports class-specific environmental-zone criteria; light gas vehicles use Euro 6 table-2 limits. Exemptions and vehicle documentation remain qualified. No named municipal boundary is asserted.

Read chapter 2 section 8: remain and assist regardless of fault, information/police duties, moving an obstructing vehicle with stricter serious-injury evidence rules. Read chapter 3 sections 51 and 57: move breakdowns promptly, warn sufficiently early without a universal triangle distance. Reused same-day checks of speed/control and crossing/parking duties for the mixed journey; its earlier-module rules remain unchanged.
Inspected TS/TRV results did not establish the complete current 50/70 comparison and reciprocal duties. The current statutory provisions give exact primary legal support.

text: Interpret signs, panels, markings and signals together, including authorised directions.

Follow the traffic instructions that apply to you. Where an instruction differs from a general traffic rule, the instruction governs. Chapter 3 sections 14, 43, 46, 50, 65–66 and chapter 4 sections 10–10d support speed/control, safe movement, securing stationary vehicles, signalling obligations and occupant protection. Relevant current provisions checked; future unrelated amendments not applied.

Current chapter 2 §§2–4 supports precedence. Chapter 3 §§5,7,9–11,14–20 supports yielding, lane choice, line restrictions, safe speed, defaults and keeping junctions clear. Chapter 9 §1 motorway defaults retained. Future unrelated amendments not applied.
The general Swedish following-distance duty requires adaptation to avoid rear collision on slowing/stopping, without specifying a fixed three-second interval.

Chapter 3 §§18–29, 43–44 and 60–66 checked: exit rule, priority-road/no-lane-change exception, roundabout entry, acceleration-lane join, turning position, mutual adaptation, controlled/uncontrolled crossings and signalling. Current provisions used; unrelated future amendments not applied. The short acceleration-lane companion explanation is explicitly sourced to §23.

Chapter 2 §1 and chapter 3 §§15, 21, 45–55 and 58 support consideration, bus departures at limits up to 50 km/h, reversing, stopping/parking distances, unmarked bus-stop extent, vehicle security, doors and the weekday 24-hour/disc rules. Chapter 8 §§1–1a confirms special-street rules; chapter 10 §1 allows lawful local parking arrangements. Current provisions used; future amendments unrelated to this chapter are not applied.
Special bus-stop departure duty at road limits ≤50; no such special duty at 70, but safe-entry and speed-adaptation/cooperation duties remain.

Chapter 2 §§2 and 7 supports authorised directions and railway approach/entry duties. Chapter 3 §§2, 7, 11, 14–15, 21, 23, 30–43 and 51 supports spacing, lane choice, continuous lines, visibility, meeting, overtaking restrictions and exceptions, joining/exiting and unavoidable stops. Chapter 4 §20 confirms vehicle-combination limits; the version effective on the check date is used, not the amendment effective 1 December 2026. Chapter 9 §§1–2 confirms motorway/expressway eligibility and movement restrictions. No legal exception is treated as proof that a manoeuvre is safe.
Turning/leaving road must protect oncoming and same-direction/rear traffic; turning around must avoid danger/obstruction; motorway/expressway turnaround and reversing prohibited.

Chapter 3 §§1, 14–15 and 68–72 supports fitness, visibility-based speed and lighting duties, including main-beam dazzle restrictions and fog-light combinations. Chapter 4 §10e supports the equipment-use limits; §§18a–18d confirms the winter-tyre framework for the ordinary light-vehicle case. Current provisions are used, not future amendments.

Chapter 3 §§78–83 confirms securing, unobstructed controls/signals and projection marking. Chapter 4 §§15–17 confirms ordinary width/length restrictions and exemptions. Chapter 4 §20 version applicable before 1 December 2026 supports the scoped 80/40/30 trailer limits; future amendment not applied early. Chapter 3 §14 supports appropriate speed.
Safe-speed adaptation depends on road/weather/visibility/load and foreseeable stopping distance.

Chapter 3 sections 2 and 14 support following distance and safe speed/control. Chapter 4 sections 22–24a supports class-specific environmental-zone criteria; light gas vehicles use Euro 6 table-2 limits. Exemptions and vehicle documentation remain qualified. No named municipal boundary is asserted.

Read chapter 2 section 8: remain and assist regardless of fault, information/police duties, moving an obstructing vehicle with stricter serious-injury evidence rules. Read chapter 3 sections 51 and 57: move breakdowns promptly, warn sufficiently early without a universal triangle distance. Reused same-day checks of speed/control and crossing/parking duties for the mixed journey; its earlier-module rules remain unchanged.

text: Interpret signs, panels, markings and signals together, including authorised directions.

Follow the traffic instructions that apply to you. Where an instruction differs from a general traffic rule, the instruction governs. A steady traffic-light indication takes precedence over a yield or stop sign; a police officer's direction takes precedence over the rules and ordinary traffic instructions. Explain how observation, speed, reaction, braking, grip and following space affect your options.

A police officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals, signs and general rules.

Chapter 3 sections 14, 43, 46, 50, 65–66 and chapter 4 sections 10–10d support speed/control, safe movement, securing stationary vehicles, signalling obligations and occupant protection. Relevant current provisions checked; future unrelated amendments not applied.

The general Swedish following-distance duty requires adaptation to avoid rear collision on slowing/stopping, without specifying a fixed three-second interval.

Chapter 3 §§18–29, 43–44 and 60–66 checked: exit rule, priority-road/no-lane-change exception, roundabout entry, acceleration-lane join, turning position, mutual adaptation, controlled/uncontrolled crossings and signalling. Chapter 2 §§2 and 7 supports authorised directions and railway approach/entry duties. Chapter 3 §§2, 7, 11, 14–15, 21, 23, 30–43 and 51 supports spacing, lane choice, continuous lines, visibility, meeting, overtaking restrictions and exceptions, joining/exiting and unavoidable stops. Chapter 9 §§1–2 confirms motorway/expressway eligibility and movement restrictions. No legal exception is treated as proof that a manoeuvre is safe.
Turning/leaving road must protect oncoming and same-direction/rear traffic; turning around must avoid danger/obstruction; motorway/expressway turnaround and reversing prohibited.

Chapter 3 §§1, 14–15 and 68–72 supports fitness, visibility-based speed and lighting duties, including main-beam dazzle restrictions and fog-light combinations. Chapter 4 §10e supports the equipment-use limits; §§18a–18d confirms the winter-tyre framework for the ordinary light-vehicle case. Current provisions are used, not future amendments.

Chapter 3 §§78–83 confirms securing, unobstructed controls/signals and projection marking. Chapter 4 §§15–17 confirms ordinary width/length restrictions and exemptions. Chapter 4 §20 version applicable before 1 December 2026 supports the scoped 80/40/30 trailer limits; future amendment not applied early. Chapter 3 §14 supports appropriate speed.
Safe-speed adaptation depends on road/weather/visibility/load and foreseeable stopping distance.

Chapter 3 sections 2 and 14 support following distance and safe speed/control. Chapter 4 sections 22–24a supports class-specific environmental-zone criteria; light gas vehicles use Euro 6 table-2 limits. Exemptions and vehicle documentation remain qualified. No named municipal boundary is asserted.

Read chapter 2 section 8: remain and assist regardless of fault, information/police duties, moving an obstructing vehicle with stricter serious-injury evidence rules. Read chapter 3 sections 51 and 57: move breakdowns promptly, warn sufficiently early without a universal triangle distance. Reused same-day checks of speed/control and crossing/parking duties for the mixed journey; its earlier-module rules remain unchanged.
Inspected TS/TRV results did not establish the complete current 50/70 comparison and reciprocal duties. The current statutory provisions give exact primary legal support.

text: Interpret signs, panels, markings and signals together, including authorised directions.

Follow the traffic instructions that apply to you. Where an instruction differs from a general traffic rule, the instruction governs. A steady traffic-light indication takes precedence over a yield or stop sign; a police officer's direction takes precedence over the rules and ordinary traffic instructions. This is not a rule that a green signal cancels every other restriction. Authorised guards also give traffic directions that must be followed. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §§2–4

Read the current signs and conditions rather than selecting a speed from the road’s appearance. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §17, chapter 4 §20 and chapter 9 §1

Safe-speed adaptation depends on road/weather/visibility/load and foreseeable stopping distance.
